title: Manipuri Short Film ‘Interlude’ Selected for Kolkata International Film Festival 2026 Competition
summary: Manipuri filmmaker Priyakanta Laishram's short film Interlude has been selected for the National Competition on Short Films at KIFF 2026 and will have its world premiere.
body:
IMPHAL, November 19: Manipuri filmmaker Priyakanta Laishram’s short film Interlude has been selected for the National Competition on Short Films at the 2026 Kolkata International Film Festival (KIFF), where it is scheduled to have its world premiere.

The selection marks a notable achievement for Manipuri cinema, as Interlude is the only film from Manipur featured in the festival’s Shorts Competition Section. It will compete alongside other selected films at the international festival, which is accredited by the International Federation of Film Producers Associations (FIAPF).

Directed by Priyakanta Laishram and produced by Roushil Singla under the banner of Priyakanta Productions, the short film is set against the backdrop of a relief camp in Manipur. Its narrative explores the human experiences of displacement, focusing on everyday encounters, personal relationships and moments of vulnerability among people living amid uncertainty.

**A Different Approach to Filmmaking**

Interlude represents an experimental approach to filmmaking by Laishram, who has chosen a black-and-white visual treatment and a 4:3 aspect ratio. The film also avoids a conventional background musical score, instead relying on natural ambience, location sound and silence to shape its narrative.

Speaking about the creative approach, Laishram described the project as an experiment in both subject and filmmaking technique. He said he wanted to explore a different cinematic language rather than repeat familiar approaches.

"I believe every film should teach you something new and push you to discover another dimension of your craft," he said, expressing his interest in continuing to explore different ways of storytelling.

**Cast Includes Relief Camp Residents**

The film features Narmada Shougaijam, Baggee Tonjam, Parihanba Thingnam, Ramesh Atom, Ramva Leishangthem and Shorojinii Rajkumari in key roles.

It also includes residents of the Sawombung and Sajiwa relief camps, bringing the experiences and presence of people living in relief settings into the film's narrative.

By placing the story within a relief camp, the film turns its attention towards the everyday human experiences behind displacement, moving beyond a purely event-based depiction of the situation.

**Recognition for Manipuri Cinema**

The selection of Interlude for the national short film competition at KIFF provides an important platform for the film and its creative team to present their work before a wider audience.

Its world premiere at the festival will mark its first major festival presentation. Being the only Manipuri entry in the Shorts Competition Section also brings attention to filmmaking from Manipur and the stories emerging from the state.

The selection highlights the potential of regional cinema to present local experiences and perspectives through different cinematic approaches, while bringing stories rooted in Manipur to audiences beyond the Northeast.

For Priyakanta Laishram and the team behind Interlude, the festival selection represents an opportunity to introduce their work to a broader film community and contribute to the visibility of Manipuri cinema on a national and international platform.
author: Mirror Lilong Desk
